literal: At the beginning of Wuping he was palace investigating censor; he was transferred to attendant of the Secretariat and awaited edicts at the Wulin Hall.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuping he served as palace investigating censor, then was transferred to secretariat attendant and awaited edicts at the Wulin Hall.

literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was attendant to the crown prince and director of composition.
idiomatic: Under Sui, in the Kaihuang era, he was attendant to the crown prince and director of composition.

literal: He compiled the Book of Later Wei in ninety-two juan, which greatly captured the historiographic form; his own time praised its excellence.
idiomatic: He compiled the Book of Later Wei in ninety-two juan, which caught the historiographic manner well; contemporaries praised it.

literal: Cui Quan, styled Changru, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
idiomatic: Cui Quan, styled Changru, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

literal: His father Xiu was Wei minister of the seven armories; posthumously granted vice director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: His father Xiu had been Wei minister of the seven armories and was posthumously granted vice director of the secretariat.

literal: Quan was of imposing stature and handsome appearance, skilled in deportment; from youth he had reputation, and men of the time knew him.
idiomatic: Quan was tall and striking, skilled in bearing; even in youth he had a name, and his contemporaries knew him.

literal: At first he was a dirge-bearer for Emperor Shizong of Wei; upon leaving office he was made erudite of the Imperial Academy.
idiomatic: He began as a dirge-bearer for Emperor Shizong of Wei and, on leaving that post, was made erudite of the Imperial Academy.

literal: In the Yongan era, for an offense he was dismissed and returned to his home district.
idiomatic: In the Yongan era he was dismissed for an offense and returned to his home district.

literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous cause at Xindu, Quan came to join him.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the righteous cause at Xindu, Quan came to join him.

literal: Gao Huan saw him and was greatly pleased, making him advisory aide.
idiomatic: Gao Huan saw him and was greatly pleased, appointing him advisory aide.

literal: Soon he was removed and made attendant of the Yellow Gate; he was transferred to general and right grand master for splendid happiness.
idiomatic: Soon he was made attendant of the yellow gate, then transferred to general and right grand master for splendid happiness.

literal: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, they deliberated on deposing and enthroning.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, they deliberated on deposing and enthroning.

literal: Grand Master of the Stud Qi Jun lavishly praised the Prince of Putai as worthy and bright, fit to be lord of the altars of soil and grain.
idiomatic: Grand master of the stud Qi Jun lavishly praised the Prince of Putai as worthy and bright, fit to be lord of the realm.

literal: Quan said: "If he were bright and sage, he could naturally await our Prince Gao and slowly ascend the throne.
idiomatic: Quan said, "If he were bright and sage, he could naturally await our Prince Gao and slowly take the throne.

literal: Since he was enthroned by rebellious barbarians, how can he still act as Son of Heaven?
idiomatic: Since rebellious barbarians enthroned him, how can he still be Son of Heaven?

literal: If we follow Jun's words, under what righteous name does the royal army march?
idiomatic: If we follow Jun's counsel, what righteous name does the royal army march under?

literal: " Thereupon both the Zhongxing and Putai [emperors] were deposed, and the Prince of Pingyang was enthroned in their stead.
idiomatic: " Thereupon both the Zhongxing and Putai rulers were deposed, and the Prince of Pingyang was enthroned instead.

literal: For merit in raising the righteous cause he was enfeoffed Duke of Wucheng County with a fief of fourteen hundred households; he advanced to general of chariots and cavalry and left grand master for splendid happiness, and still headed the Yellow Gate office.
idiomatic: For merit in raising the righteous cause he was enfeoffed duke of Wucheng County with a fief of fourteen hundred households, advanced to general of chariots and cavalry and left grand master for splendid happiness, and still headed the yellow gate office.

literal: Quan dwelt in the gate office, relying on his share in the righteous banner, and was rather self-conceited and unrestrained.
idiomatic: Quan served in the gate office, trusting in his share in the righteous banner, and grew rather proud and unrestrained.

literal: Soon for corruption he was impeached by the censorate; he fled home, and only after an amnesty did he emerge.
idiomatic: Soon the censorate impeached him for corruption; he fled home and emerged only after an amnesty.

literal: Gao Huan, because Quan had originally joined the righteous banner, restored him to the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: Because Quan had originally joined the righteous banner, Gao Huan restored him to the yellow gate.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was lecturer-in-attendance and supervised the palace library.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was lecturer-in-attendance and supervised the palace library.

literal: Soon he was removed and made governor of Xu Province; he was given three hundred retainers of Guangzong and a thousand retainers of Qinghe.
idiomatic: Soon he was made governor of Xu Province, with three hundred Guangzong retainers and a thousand Qinghe retainers granted him.

literal: Quan was by nature arrogant and overbearing; he favored his concubine Lady Feng and lent her his punitive authority, taking and accepting as she pleased — government and customs were not established.
idiomatic: Quan was arrogant by nature; he favored his concubine Lady Feng and lent her his punitive authority, so she extorted at will and local government collapsed.

literal: When Quan was first regular attendant, he sought someone to compile the imperial diary.
idiomatic: When Quan was first regular attendant, he sought someone to compile the imperial diary.

literal: Someone said: "Wei Shou would do.
idiomatic: Someone said, "Wei Shou would do.

literal: " Quan said: "Shou is but a frivolous fellow.
idiomatic: " Quan said, "Shou is nothing but a frivolous fellow.

literal: " He brought in Zu Hongxun instead.
idiomatic: " He brought in Zu Hongxun instead.

literal: Once he held a pivotal post, he also had Lu Yuanming replace Shou as secretariat gentleman; from this Shou bore a grudge.
idiomatic: Once he held a pivotal post, he also had Lu Yuanming replace Shou as secretariat gentleman — from this Shou bore a grudge.

literal: When Shou went on a mission to hire Liang and passed through Xu Province, Quan equipped the full insignia of a governor to escort him and had a man convey word to Wei: "Do not wonder at the many guards — it is the power of classical learning.
idiomatic: When Shou went on a mission to Liang and passed through Xu Province, Quan sent him off with a governor's full train of insignia and had a man tell Wei, "Do not wonder at the many guards — it is the power of classical learning.

literal: " Shou replied: "Tell Governor Cui of Xu: for merit in raising the righteous cause, what classical learning is there!
idiomatic: " Shou replied, "Tell Governor Cui of Xu: merit in raising the righteous cause — what has that to do with classical learning!

literal: " Quan, trusting in his clan's long-standing eminence, was especially displeased at this remark.
idiomatic: " Quan, trusting in his clan's long eminence, was especially displeased at this remark.

literal: Shou seized on an old resentment and therefore used this to humiliate him.
idiomatic: Shou seized on an old resentment and used the occasion to humiliate him.

literal: When he left the province he was made minister of the seven armories and chief clan elder of Qinghe.
idiomatic: When he left the province he was made minister of the seven armories and chief clan elder of Qinghe.

literal: Li Hun of Zhao commandery once feasted a gathering of eminent men; poetry and wine were in full clamor when Quan arrived late — the whole company ceased conversation.
idiomatic: Li Hun of Zhao commandery once feasted a gathering of eminent men; poetry and wine were in full clamor when Quan arrived late — and the whole table fell silent.

literal: Zheng Boyou sighed and said: "Eight feet in height, a face like carved in relief, a cough like the boom of a great bell, a thousand scrolls stored in the breast — how could men not fear and submit!"
idiomatic: Zheng Boyou sighed and said, "Eight feet tall, a face carved in relief, a cough like a great bell, a thousand scrolls in the breast — how could one not fear and submit!"

literal: Quan often prided himself on his registered pedigree and said to Lu Yuanming: "Among the great houses under Heaven, only you and I; Bo, Cui, Zhao, and Li — what are they for!
idiomatic: Quan often prided himself on his registered pedigree and said to Lu Yuanming, "Among the great houses under Heaven, only you and I; the Bo, Cui, Zhao, and Li clans — what are they worth!

literal: " Cui Xian heard of it and bore a grudge.
idiomatic: " Cui Xian heard of it and bore a grudge.

literal: After Gao Huan's burial, Quan again spoke in private: "Can this yellow-bearded boy bear heavy responsibility?
idiomatic: After Gao Huan's burial, Quan again spoke in private, "Can this yellow-bearded boy bear heavy responsibility?

literal: " Cui Xian's cousin by marriage Li Shen heard of it.
idiomatic: " Cui Xian's cousin by marriage Li Shen heard of it.

literal: Quan's remark was reported to Xian.
idiomatic: Quan's remark was reported to Xian.

literal: Xian memorialized Emperor Wen, and Quan's court attendance was cut off.
idiomatic: Xian memorialized Emperor Wen, and Quan's court attendance was cut off.

literal: Quan wanted to bow by the roadside; Emperor Wen flared in anger and said: "Yellow-bearded boy — what is there to bow to!
idiomatic: Quan wanted to bow by the roadside; Emperor Wen flared in anger and said, "Yellow-bearded boy — what is there to bow to!

literal: " Thereupon Quan was shackled and taken to Jinyang for interrogation.
idiomatic: " Thereupon Quan was shackled and taken to Jinyang for interrogation.

literal: Quan would not confess; Xian cited Xing Zicai of the Ministry of Justice as witness, and Zicai held that there had been no such words.
idiomatic: Quan would not confess; Xian cited Xing Zicai of the ministry of justice as witness, and Zicai maintained that no such words had been spoken.

literal: Quan, in detention, said to Zicai: "Do you know my mind is set on Taqiu?
idiomatic: Quan, in detention, said to Zicai, "Do you know my mind is set on Taqiu?

literal: " Zicai went out and told Quan's son Zhan: "Your father's intent surely is to ally by marriage with Chen Yuankang.
idiomatic: " Zicai went out and told Quan's son Zhan, "Your father's intent surely is to ally by marriage with Chen Yuankang.

literal: " Zhan had a daughter; he thereupon betrothed her to Yuankang's son and sought [release for] his father.
idiomatic: " Zhan had a daughter; he thereupon betrothed her to Yuankang's son and sought his father's release.

literal: Yuankang spoke for him to Emperor Wen, saying: "Cui Quan's renown has long been weighty; one must not put him to death over private words.
idiomatic: Yuankang spoke for him to Emperor Wen, saying, "Cui Quan's renown has long been weighty; he must not be put to death over private words.

literal: " Emperor Wen said: "If his life is spared, he should still be banished to the far marches.
idiomatic: " Emperor Wen said, "If his life is spared, he should still be banished to the far marches.

literal: " Yuankang said: "If Quan is on the frontier, he may yet defect abroad.
idiomatic: " Yuankang said, "If Quan is on the frontier, he may yet defect abroad.

literal: To supply a worthy enemy with a talented man is not fitting.
idiomatic: To supply the enemy with a man of talent is not fitting.

literal: " Emperor Wen said: "Since he has the crime of Jigui, might he still be sent to corvée labor?
idiomatic: " Emperor Wen said, "Since he has the crime of Jigui, might he still be sent to corvée labor?

literal: " Yuankang said: "I once read the biography of Cui Yan and regretted that Wei Wu was not magnanimous.
idiomatic: " Yuankang said, "I once read the biography of Cui Yan and regretted that Wei Wu was not magnanimous.

literal: If Quan dies in the labor camp, will later ages not say that Your Lordship killed him after all?
idiomatic: If Quan dies in the labor camp, will later ages not say that you killed him after all?

literal: " Emperor Wen said: "Then what is to be done?
idiomatic: " Emperor Wen said, "Then what is to be done?

literal: " Yuankang said: "Cui Quan deserves death — court and countryside alike know it; if Your Lordship can temper severity with leniency and especially lighten his punishment, then benevolent virtue will shine the brighter and all under Heaven will turn their hearts to you.
idiomatic: " Yuankang said, "Cui Quan deserves death — court and countryside alike know it; if you can temper severity with leniency and especially lighten his punishment, benevolent virtue will shine the brighter and all under Heaven will turn their hearts to you.

literal: " Thereupon he was released.
idiomatic: " Thereupon he was released.

literal: Quan came forward to audience to offer thanks; Emperor Wen was still angry and said: "Though I am unworthy, I shamefully bear great responsibility — yet you named me 'yellow-bearded boy.' Metal and stone may wear away; this saying is hard to extinguish!"
idiomatic: Quan came forward to offer thanks; Emperor Wen was still angry and said, "Though I am unworthy, I shamefully bear great responsibility — yet you named me 'yellow-bearded boy.' Metal and stone may wear away; this saying is hard to extinguish!"

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was made palace attendant and supervised the imperial diary.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was made palace attendant and supervised the imperial diary.

literal: At the time of the abdication and succession he took part in managing ritual; he was separately enfeoffed Baron of Xinfeng County with a fief of two hundred households, which he turned over to his ninth younger brother Yue.
idiomatic: At the abdication and succession he took part in managing ritual; he was separately enfeoffed baron of Xinfeng County with a fief of two hundred households, which he turned over to his ninth younger brother Yue.

literal: Throughout Quan's clan, marriages were all of the finest official families; rites for auspicious and inauspicious occasions were praised by the age.
idiomatic: Throughout Quan's clan, marriages were all into the finest official families; rites for auspicious and inauspicious occasions were praised in his day.

literal: Empress Dowager Lou took Quan's younger sister as consort for the Prince of Boling and charged the palace envoy: "Use good ceremonial forms — do not let the Cui family laugh at others.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Lou took Quan's younger sister as consort for the Prince of Boling and charged the palace envoy, "Use proper ceremonial forms — do not let the Cui family laugh at others.

literal: " On the wedding night Emperor Wenxuan raised his cup and prayed: "May the new bride bear sons, be filial and obedient, rich and noble.
idiomatic: " On the wedding night Emperor Wenxuan raised his cup and prayed, "May the new bride bear sons, be filial and obedient, rich and noble.

literal: " Quan submitted: "Filial obedience comes from my clan; wealth and honor are grace from Your Majesty."
idiomatic: " Quan submitted, "Filial obedience comes from my clan; wealth and honor are grace from Your Majesty."

literal: In the fifth year he went out as governor of Eastern Yan Province, again taking Lady Feng's retainers with him.
idiomatic: In the fifth year he went out as governor of Eastern Yan Province, again taking Lady Feng's retainers with him.

literal: Quan soon suffered hemiplegia, while Lady Feng was arrogant and unrestrained; her taking and accepting lay in disorder, and the censorate impeached them — Quan and she were both summoned to the minister of justice.
idiomatic: Quan soon suffered hemiplegia, while Lady Feng grew arrogant and unrestrained; her bribes lay in disorder, and the censorate impeached them — Quan and she were both summoned before the minister of justice.

literal: Soon there came a separate edict; Feng was beheaded in the market.
idiomatic: Soon a separate edict came down; Feng was beheaded in the market.

literal: Quan died of illness in prison at age sixty-one.
idiomatic: Quan died of illness in prison at age sixty-one.

literal: Quan read widely among books and also had literary talent; from the enthronement in the Zhongxing era down to Emperor Wu, most edicts, mandates, memorials, and proclamations were Quan's work.
idiomatic: Quan read widely and had literary talent; from the Zhongxing enthronement down to Emperor Wu, most edicts, mandates, memorials, and proclamations were his work.

literal: Yet by nature he was extravagant and proud, sunk in wealth and women; among his brothers he could not fully achieve harmonious kinship — public opinion reproached him for this.
idiomatic: Yet by nature he was extravagant and proud, sunk in wealth and women; among his brothers he could not fully achieve harmonious kinship — and public opinion reproached him for it.

literal: Quan had long been at odds with Wei Shou; once Shou came to monopolize the national history, Quan feared slander and therefore flattered him, saying: "In old times there was Ban Gu; today there is Master Wei.
idiomatic: Quan had long been at odds with Wei Shou; once Shou came to monopolize the national history, Quan feared slander and flattered him, saying, "In old times there was Ban Gu; today there is Master Wei.

literal: " Shou smiled, yet his resentment did not lift.
idiomatic: " Shou smiled, yet his resentment did not lift.

literal: His son Zhan succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Zhan succeeded.

literal: Zhan, styled Yantong, was bright and studied hard; he had literary sensibility, skilled deportment, a lofty and striking mien, and did not speak idly.
idiomatic: Zhan, styled Yantong, was bright and studied hard; he had literary sensibility, skilled bearing, a lofty and striking mien, and did not speak idly.

literal: At fifteen the governor Gao Ang summoned him to serve as chief clerk; the Duke of Qinghe, Yue, recruited him as libationer of the western pavilion of the open government.
idiomatic: At fifteen Governor Gao Ang summoned him as chief clerk; the Duke of Qinghe, Yue, recruited him as libationer of the western pavilion of the open government.

literal: Cui Xian was commandant of justice; he memorialized to remove [Zhan] as censor — he was taken in for talent and reputation, which was not to Xian's liking.
idiomatic: Cui Xian was commandant of justice; he memorialized to appoint Zhan censor — he was taken in for talent and reputation, which Xian did not favor.

literal: When Gao Huan entered court and returned to Jinyang, [Zhan] was summoned together with the Prince of Beihai Xi to attend in company; both became guest-friends to the sons.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan entered court and returned to Jinyang, Zhan was summoned together with the Prince of Beihai Xi to attend in company; both became companion-friends to the sons.

literal: He then served as middle army aide in the chancellor's government and was transferred to chief clerk.
idiomatic: He then served as middle army aide in the chancellor's government and was transferred to chief clerk.

literal: When Emperor Wen died the death was kept secret; Emperor Wenxuan ordered Zhan concurrently to serve as marshal of the chancellor's government and go to Ye.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died the death was kept secret; Emperor Wenxuan ordered Zhan concurrently to serve as marshal of the chancellor's government and go to Ye.

literal: Emperor Xiaojing of Wei, on the Human Day, ascended the Cloud Dragon Gate; his father Quan attended the feast, and [the emperor] also ordered Zhan to draw near the imperial seat; he too had a poem in response to the imperial command, and [the emperor] asked Xing Shao and the others: "How does this poem compare with his father's?
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaojing of Wei, on the Human Day, ascended the Cloud Dragon Gate; his father Quan attended the feast, and the emperor also ordered Zhan to draw near the imperial seat; he too had a poem in response to the imperial command, and the emperor asked Xing Shao and the others, "How does this poem compare with his father's?

literal: " All said: "Quan is broad, elegant, and grand; Zhan's tone is fresh and clear — both are crowns among poets.
idiomatic: " All said, "Quan is broad, elegant, and grand; Zhan's tone is fresh and clear — both crown the poets of the age.

literal: " When the feast ended they sighed in admiration together, all saying: "Today's banquet was alike for the father and son Cui Zhan."
idiomatic: " When the feast ended they sighed in admiration together, all saying, "Today's banquet belonged alike to father and son, the Cui Zhan pair."

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he concurrently served as bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel of the parallel province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he concurrently served as bureau director in the ministry of personnel of the parallel province.

literal: Soon he entered mourning; on mourning's end he was summoned as aide to the minister of state.
idiomatic: Soon he entered mourning; when mourning ended he was summoned as aide to the minister of state.

literal: Yang Yin wished to bring Zhan in as secretariat vice director.
idiomatic: Yang Yin wished to bring Zhan in as secretariat vice director.

literal: At the time Lu Sidao was on duty in the Secretariat; he therefore asked Sidao: "These days I am overwhelmed with affairs and have not seen Cui Zhan's literary talent at all; you are on intimate terms with him and ought by rights to know him well.
idiomatic: At the time Lu Sidao was on duty in the secretariat; he therefore asked Sidao, "These days I am overwhelmed with affairs and have not seen Cui Zhan's literary talent at all; you are on intimate terms with him and ought by rights to know him well.

literal: " Sidao answered: "Cui Zhan's literary phrasing is truly praiseworthy, but the world values his romantic air, and therefore his talent is overshadowed.
idiomatic: " Sidao answered, "Cui Zhan's literary phrasing is truly praiseworthy, but the world values his romantic air, and therefore his talent is overshadowed.

literal: " Yin said: "This remark has reason.
idiomatic: " Yin said, "This remark has reason.

literal: " He thereupon memorialized to employ him.
idiomatic: " He thereupon memorialized to employ him.

literal: Once the matter had been carried out.
idiomatic: Once the matter had been carried out.

literal: Yin again said: "In Jin times Pei Zan was secretariat gentleman; his spirit was lofty and far-reaching — each time he passed in and out of the forbidden gate the night guards would soberly stir.
idiomatic: Yin again said, "In Jin times Pei Zan was secretariat gentleman; his spirit was lofty and far-reaching — each time he passed in and out of the forbidden gate the night guards would soberly stir.

literal: Master Cui's imposing appearance should likewise be no disgrace to Master Pei."
idiomatic: Master Cui's imposing appearance should likewise be no disgrace to Master Pei."

literal: Zhan was by nature terse and proud; he prided himself on talent and pedigree; those with whom he associated were all men of name and standing in the age.
idiomatic: Zhan was terse and proud by nature; he prided himself on talent and pedigree; those with whom he associated were all men of name and standing in the age.

literal: While at the Censorate he constantly had food sent to his residence, furnished with every delicacy; in a separate room he dined alone, comporting himself at ease.
idiomatic: While at the censorate he constantly had food sent to his residence, furnished with every delicacy; in a separate room he dined alone, comporting himself at ease.

literal: There was a man of Hedong surnamed Pei who was also a censor; he watched for Zhan's mealtime and went to visit him.
idiomatic: There was a man of Hedong surnamed Pei who was also a censor; he watched for Zhan's mealtime and went to visit him.

literal: Zhan did not converse with him, nor did he order chopsticks and spoon.
idiomatic: Zhan did not converse with him, nor did he offer chopsticks and spoon.

literal: Pei sat watching until Zhan finished eating and withdrew.
idiomatic: Pei sat watching until Zhan finished eating and withdrew.

literal: The next day Pei brought his own chopsticks and spoon and ate and drank to his heart's content.
idiomatic: The next day Pei brought his own chopsticks and spoon and ate and drank to his heart's content.

literal: Zhan then said to Pei: "At first I did not summon you to eat, nor did I speak with you — yet you could disregard petty restraint. By nature
idiomatic: Zhan then said to Pei, "At first I did not summon you to eat, nor did I speak with you — yet you could disregard petty restraint. Your disposition
